text:
jamal: Hey team — kicking off the CatalystAI joint benchmark. Partner is focused on perf/W and peak throughput for their NimbleX boards. Want to align on scope, test matrix, and a public-friendly writeup timeline. Who can own the infra-side runbook?

mira: I can take the ML test matrix (models, seq lengths, quant profiles). Thinking: Llama2-13B FP16, MPT-7B-8K q4_0 and a 70B opt-lite baseline. Sweep seq: 128/512/2048.

oliver: I can do runtime/kernel tuning notes and provide perf knobs. We should instrument kernel timings + memory sampling. Need HW counters from Catalyst — can they enable PCIe power telemetry?

priya: Marketing wants a joint blog + datasheet. Target publish 3 weeks after runs finish. We'll need validated numbers and reproducible commands. Also list of disclaimers.

jamal: Good. @tanya can you own the CI runners and artifacts (logs, perf traces, raw telemetry upload)? We'll ask Catalyst for an SFTP and a signed checksum manifest.

tanya: Yep. I'll spin dedicated CI pools in our staging region, with tuned driver + kernel versions. Need exact kernel build from Catalyst (they mentioned 5.19-rc with some patches). Share before EOD.

mira: For fidelity, let's include both steady-state throughput and a latency tail test. Proposed metrics: throughput (tokens/s), perf/W (tokens/s/W), p95 latency for 32-token responses. Also KV-cache warm vs cold.

oliver: Agree. For kernel tuning, I'll try: pinned IRQs, NUMA-aware allocator, and prefetcher tweaks. I'll document exact sysctl + modprobe flags. Example run command we'll publish:```bash
python run_bench.py --model llama2-13b --quant fp16 --seq 2048 --batch 1 --profile /tmp/out
```

jamal: Partner preconditions: they asked for a non-embargoed summary to share with their partners but want the raw telemetry private until joint signoff. We'll keep numbers internal until signoff.

priya: Can we get a small set of reproducible commands and a docker image tag for the blog? That helps legal sign-off and reproducibility claims.

mira: I'll bake a dockerfile with pinned deps and add an eval harness to compute tokens/s and perf/W using an external wattmeter hook. Need to know what wattmeter model they're using (PowerMon v2?).

jamal: I'll confirm with Catalyst — they said PowerMon v2 and will provide csv export + timestamps.

bench-bot: scheduled run created: bench-catalyst-3301112222 — earliest window 2026-04-08T02:00Z to 2026-04-10T08:00Z. Notifying eng-runtime & eng-ml.

oliver: Quick question: do we standardize on the same compiler flags and CUDA/cuplib versions? Small differences change perf/W. I suggest we fix: CUDA 12.3, cuBLAS/cuDNN pinned, and GCC 12.2. Documented in runbook.

tanya: noted. I'll lock base image to those versions and snapshot AMIs. Also will capture `nvidia-smi` output and kernel dmesg at start/end.

mira: For datasets: use same synthetic tokens plus 2 real prompt sets (codegen and convo). We'll report separate breakdowns.

priya: Once we have draft numbers, I'll prep a one-page joint summary with charts: perf/W vs batch size, throughput vs seq length, thermal throttling notes. Leave room for Catalyst quotes.

jamal: Action items recap: Mira -> test matrix & docker, Oliver -> kernel tuning doc & knobs, Tanya -> CI runners + AMIs, Priya -> comms + blog outline, Jamal -> partner coordination + telemetry access. Targets: telemetry access by 2026-04-01, runs complete by 2026-04-10, draft publish assets by 2026-04-24.

oliver: I'll also collect flamegraphs for token-generation path and produce a short list of top-3 kernel hotspots to hand to Catalyst for driver patches.

mira: One more: include a small A/B with our batching cache enabled vs disabled to show tail latency vs overall perf/W tradeoffs.

jamal: Perfect. I'll send Catalyst the runbook skeleton and request the kernel patch diffs. Thanks all — will post updates here as Catalyst responds. :thumbsup:

priya: :rocket:

bench-bot: reminder scheduled: bench-catalyst-3301112222 will start in 72 hours.
